doc.title: Jon Weber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 2, 2012

title: University of Wisconsin Milwaukee, Plan B majors, bypassing jazz education
summary: He studied at UW Milwaukee with many majors as a fallback, played piano constantly, missed formal jazz education, and wrote charts for others and ran a quintet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So I’m not likely to see you in an ad for a music college saying, “You should come here because my career really started here.” You were able to sort of bypass that whole jazz education at a college level thing or not?

Yes. Well I ended up auditing a number of classes when I went to the University of Wisconsin Milwaukee, I went for four years and I had like eight different majors. Because I thought the voice of reason — my parents — entered into it. They said, “You know we like your music but you need something to think about, the Plan B.”

You know? And I said okay, accounting and mathematics, I’m no good at that, what else, oh jeez. You know, but there would be the piano over in the corner and I’d think okay I’ll play for five minutes. Four hours later I was still playing. I managed to get decent enough grades and I thought I’m going to be a piano player the rest of my life, as I warned my mother at age three — “I’m going to be a piano player and this is what I’m going to pursue.” But no the jazz academic route is something that I missed entirely. I ended up writing charts for other students. In other words I remember doing a 100-piece orchestration for a woman I had a big crush on. And sometimes I wrote big band charts for Mark Kleckley’s band once in a while. And other combos. I had a quintet who opened up for people like Pat Metheny and Buddy Rich.
